answer: Random sampling is the cheapest sybil defense. Each epoch validators publish a rate and draw a fraction of submissions from shared randomness, so no operator knows which accounts will be re-derived. Faking buys a saving per account but risks a proportional fine and bond loss; once the sampled penalty exceeds that saving, ten thousand accounts cost more than ten. Probes rest on facts a script cannot guess: the height of a willow on a slope, the steps of a terrace, water depth at a wharf at a stated hour. Each fact is gathered per identity, so costs scale with accounts and savings do not.
